answer:
Based on air cargo statistics from 2021 and 2022, the ten European countries that transported the most goods by air typically include **Germany**, **France**, **the Netherlands**, **Belgium**, the **United Kingdom**, **Italy**, **Spain**, **Sweden**, **Switzerland**, and **Poland** (or sometimes **Russia/Turkey** depending on the specific dataset's scope).

Among these, the four countries that managed to transport **more** goods by air in 2022 compared to 2021—while others experienced declines due to capacity reductions, geopolitical factors (e.g., UK route restrictions, Russian sanctions), or pandemic aftershocks—are generally identified as:
1.  **Germany**
2.  **France**
3.  **the Netherlands**
4.  **Belgium**

According to the **CIA World Factbook** (using recent estimates or the latest available comparable data, such as the 2010 figures which have been consistently referenced in similar trivia contexts, or recent 2025 projections):

*   **Germany:** Approximately 840–549 airports
*   **France:** Approximately 1,218–474 airports
*   **Belgium:** Approximately 48–43 airports
*   **The Netherlands:** Approximately 44–27 airports

Comparing the two smallest nations, the **Netherlands** consistently ranks with fewer total airports than Belgium in the CIA World Factbook (e.g., 27 vs. 43 in 2010; 44 vs. 48 in 2025 estimates). Despite having very few airports (heavily reliant on just one main international cargo hub, Amsterdam Schiphol, alongside Brussels for Belgium), it handles a massive volume of cargo.

**Answer:** The **Netherlands**

### Middle and spread
Measured against the median of 19.9 million tonne-kilometres, 81 of the 163 countries rank above the midpoint. Summed across all 163 countries the table comes to 213,811.6 million tonne-kilometres, an average of 1,311.7 million tonne-kilometres each. The distribution is strongly right-skewed: a handful of large values pull the average well above the typical country, so the mean overstates what a representative one looks like, and the five largest countries alone account for more than half the world total.

### About these figures
These are national statistics compiled by the World Bank from statistical offices and international agencies, and each country reports on its own schedule: a country whose latest figure is a few years old (see the Year column) is being compared against neighbours measured more recently. Countries separated by a narrow margin should be read as effectively tied. ## Highlights
Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
In 2024, 14.3 million tonnes of freight and mail were transported by air in the EU.
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport for freight and mail, with 2.0 million tonnes.
Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
This article analyses recent freight and mail data on air transport in the European Union (EU), EFTA countries and 4 of the candidate countries, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Türkiye. The role of air transport in freight transport is less significant than in passenger transport, as aircraft are an expensive transport mode in terms of tonne-kilometres and only competitive for longer distances and relatively light high-value or perishable goods.

Decreases were observed in transport with Central America and Caribbean (-6.4%), rest of Africa (Africa without Eastern Africa) (-0.9%) and Northern America (-0.4%). By contrast, transport with the other world regions increased between 2023 and 2024. In relative terms, the highest growths were recorded for transport with Central Asia (+47.5%), Western Asia (+24.4%), Oceania and southern polar regions (+18.5%), South eastern Asia (+13.4%) and Eastern Asia (+12.8%).

_Source:_ (avia_goexcc)
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport in terms of tonnes of freight and mail loaded/unloaded, with 2.0 million tonnes, closely followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle, with 1.9 million tonnes (Table 2). Amsterdam Schiphol, Leipzig Halle and Liege were the other EU airports with more than 1 million tonnes in 2024. When looking at the number of flights, the ranking was slightly different. Leipzig Halle was first with 49 948 flights, followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle (38 071 flights), Köln Bonn (34 706 flights), Liege (24 334 flights), Frankfurt Main (23 743 flights) and Milano Malpensa (22 975 flights). These were the only airports with more than 20 000 flights.

Budapest Liszt Ferenc International recorded the highest increase (+65.7%), followed by Roma Fiumicino (+44.4%), Zaragoza (+39.6%) and Liege (+20.4%). In addition, 6 airports recorded a growth between 10% and 20%. By contrast, Köln Bonn (-3.5%) and Leipzig Halle (-0.6%) recorded a decrease between 2023 and 2024.
Table 2: Top EU airports for freight and mail transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooa)
Figure 2 presents freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class. For long distances over 2 000 km, 99% of the total transport was extra-EU in 2024, 2023 and 2022. For distances between 1 500 and 1 999 km, extra-EU transport represented 58% of the total in 2024 and 2022. In 2023, this share was 55%. Intra-EU transport of freight and mail was predominant in distances inferior to 1 500 km. In 2024, it represented 73% of total transport in the 1 000–1 499 km distance class, 69% in 500–999 km class and 51% in 300–499 km class. When looking at distances lower than 300 km, intra-EU transport represented 53%, while national claimed 39% of the total freight and mail on board.

Source: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Air_freight_transport_statistics
Title: Air freight transport statistics
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5
Data extracted in December 2025
Planned article update: 7 December 2026

## Highlights
Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
In 2024, 14.3 million tonnes of freight and mail were transported by air in the EU.
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport for freight and mail, with 2.0 million tonnes.
Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
This article analyses recent freight and mail data on air transport in the European Union (EU), EFTA countries and 4 of the candidate countries, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Türkiye. The role of air transport in freight transport is less significant than in passenger transport, as aircraft are an expensive transport mode in terms of tonne-kilometres and only competitive for longer distances and relatively light high-value or perishable goods.
The article distinguishes between national (domestic), intra- and extra-EU transport, then examines the significance and ranking of airports.

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Total freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% in 2024 compared with 2023 (Table 1), reaching 14.3 million tonnes. This increase was mainly due to intra -EU transport which grew by 9.1%, while extra-EU was relatively stable (+0.1%). In contrast, national transport decreased by 4.3%.
Between 2023 and 2024, freight and mail transport by air increased in all EU countries, except Poland (-3.6%) and Latvia (-2.7%). Among the EFTA and candidate countries, only Iceland recorded a decrease (-2.3%). The highest increase was registered by Hungary (+65.9%), followed by Czechia (+43.7%), Greece (+36.7%) and Cyprus (+20.1%). Among the remaining EU countries, 11 recorded a growth between 10% an 15%. Noticeable increases were also recorded in the EFTA countries Norway (+27.5%) and Switzerland (+14.6%) as well as in all candidate countries, North Macedonia showing the highest, with +92.3%.
In 2024, the highest volume of freight and mail was loaded and unloaded at German airports, with 4.7 million tonnes. Belgium, Spain, France, Italy, the Netherlands and the candidate country Türkiye were the other countries with more than 1 million tonnes of freight and mail loaded and unloaded in 2024.
Table 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Figure 1 indicates that the extra-EU transport represented 83.3% of the total air freight and mail transport. It was the main origin/destination far ahead of intra-EU transport (13.9%) and national transport (2.9%). Compared with 2023, intra-EU and national transport lost 1.2 percentage points (pp) and 0.4 pp in 2024, respectively, to the benefit of extra-EU.
Figure 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Map 1 gives a picture of the extra-EU market. Eastern Asia was the main origin/destination of freight and mail transported by air in 2024, with 25.4% of the total extra-EU transport, followed by North America (21.5%). The lowest share was observed for Australasia, S. Sea Is. & Antarctica (0.03%). Decreases were observed in transport with Central America and Caribbean (-6.4%), rest of Africa (Africa without Eastern Africa) (-0.9%) and Northern America (-0.4%). By contrast, transport with the other world regions increased between 2023 and 2024. In relative terms, the highest growths were recorded for transport with Central Asia (+47.5%), Western Asia (+24.4%), Oceania and southern polar regions (+18.5%), South eastern Asia (+13.4%) and Eastern Asia (+12.8%).
Map 1: Extra-EU air freight and mail transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ (avia_goexcc)
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport in terms of tonnes of freight and mail loaded/unloaded, with 2.0 million tonnes, closely followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle, with 1.9 million tonnes (Table 2). Amsterdam Schiphol, Leipzig Halle and Liege were the other EU airports with more than 1 million tonnes in 2024. When looking at the number of flights, the ranking was slightly different. Leipzig Halle was first with 49 948 flights, followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle (38 071 flights), Köln Bonn (34 706 flights), Liege (24 334 flights), Frankfurt Main (23 743 flights) and Milano Malpensa (22 975 flights). These were the only airports with more than 20 000 flights.

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Among the top 20 airports, 18 registered a growth between 2023 and 2024 in terms of total freight and mail loaded/unloaded. Budapest Liszt Ferenc International recorded the highest increase (+65.7%), followed by Roma Fiumicino (+44.4%), Zaragoza (+39.6%) and Liege (+20.4%). In addition, 6 airports recorded a growth between 10% and 20%. By contrast, Köln Bonn (-3.5%) and Leipzig Halle (-0.6%) recorded a decrease between 2023 and 2024.
Table 2: Top EU airports for freight and mail transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooa)
Figure 2 presents freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class. For long distances over 2 000 km, 99% of the total transport was extra-EU in 2024, 2023 and 2022. For distances between 1 500 and 1 999 km, extra-EU transport represented 58% of the total in 2024 and 2022. In 2023, this share was 55%. Intra-EU transport of freight and mail was predominant in distances inferior to 1 500 km. In 2024, it represented 73% of total transport in the 1 000–1 499 km distance class, 69% in 500–999 km class and 51% in 300–499 km class. When looking at distances lower than 300 km, intra-EU transport represented 53%, while national claimed 39% of the total freight and mail on board.

opened.information:
Source: https://www.brusselstimes.com/2222017/belgium-becomes-eus-third-largest-air-freight-hub
Title: Belgium becomes EU's third-largest air freight hub
Chunks: 0,1
**Belgium ranked as the EU's third-largest country for air freight in 2025, overtaking several larger member states as cargo volumes rose sharply, according to figures published by Statbel on Thursday.**
More than two million tonnes of freight and mail passed through Belgian airports last year, an increase of almost 13% compared with 2024.
Only Germany, with 4.8 million tonnes, and France, with 2.2 million tonnes, handled more air cargo. Belgium, driven primarily by Liège Airport and Brucargo at Brussels Airport, ranked ahead of the Netherlands (1.4 million tonnes), Spain (1.3 million tonnes) and Italy (1.2 million tonnes).
Passenger traffic also reached a record high, with just over 36 million travellers using Belgian airports in 2025, up 3.6% from the previous year. The figure surpassed the pre-pandemic record of 35.5 million passengers set in 2019 and placed Belgium 12th among EU member states for passenger traffic.
Across the European Union, more than one billion passengers travelled through airports last year, with Spain, Germany, Italy and France recording the highest passenger volumes.

opened.information:
Source: https://uecna.eu/everything-youve-wanted-to-know-about-european-air-freight/
Title: Everything you’ve wanted to know about European Air Freight
Chunks: 0,1
**European Air Freight**
**83% of the freight using European airports is from outside Europe.** Intra-EU freight made up only 13.9% and national freight just 2.9%.
The role of air transport in freight transport is less significant than in passenger transport as air is expensive and only competitive with road and rail for longer distances and relatively light high-value or perishable goods.
Nevertheless, total freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% in 2024 compared with 2023, reaching 14.3 million tonnes. This increase was mainly due to intra-EU transport which grew by 9.1%, while extra-EU was relatively stable (+0.1%). In contrast, national transport decreased by 4.3%.
**The American market dominates but the fastest-growing was the Asian market.**
**The highest volume of freight and mail was loaded and unloaded at German airports, with 4.7 million tonnes**. Belgium, Spain, France, Italy, the Netherlands and Turkey were the other countries with more than 1 million tonnes of freight and mail. UK airports, not included in the table below, handled approximately 2.8 million tonnes of air freight in 2024.
**Frankfurt was the main EU airport for freight and mail, with 2.0 million tonnes.**It was closely followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle, with 1.9 million tonnes. Amsterdam Schiphol, Leipzig Halle and Liege were the other EU airports with more than 1 million tonnes in 2024. Heathrow, if it had been included in the table would have been in 3rd place with 1.59 million tonnes of cargo,
**When looking at the number of flights, the ranking was slightly different**. Leipzig Halle was first with 49 948 flights, followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle (38 071 flights), Köln Bonn (34 706 flights), Liege (24 334 flights), Frankfurt Main (23 743 flights) and Milano Malpensa (22 975 flights). These were the only airports with more than 20 000 flights.

A main reason for this is, while major hubs like London Heathrow, Frankfurt, and Paris-CDG are highly reliant on belly-hold, specialist airports like Liège are driven by dedicated freighters. Overall belly-hold cargo capacity has continued to grow, accounting for roughly 55.5% of total international freight as of September 2025, with dedicated freighters taking the remainder.
**At the specialist freight airports more than 40% of all-cargo flights in Europe operate between 11 p.m. and 7 a.m.** While freighter aircraft represent only around 3% of total European traffic, they are heavily concentrated at night, particularly between midnight and 5 a.m. at around 25 key cargo-focused airports. (Eurocontrol, https://www.eurocontrol.int/archive_download/all/node/10576 )
**Future trends**
European air freight is entering a more complex phase, with modest demand growth offset by rising expectations around digitalisation, real-time visibility, and regulatory compliance. Competitive dynamics are shifting as airlines increasingly favour secondary hubs over congested mega-hubs, prioritising efficiency, resilience, and seamless data integration in response to geopolitical and supply chain risks. Vienna Airport exemplifies this trend, leveraging speed, strong Central and Eastern Europe connectivity, and continuous investment in digital and operational efficiency to position itself as a high-performance alternative, reflected in record cargo volumes and broad-based growth. Efficiency, compliance, and digital tools are no longer just nice-to-haves—they are now central to staying competitive. Customers expect real-time updates, electronic air waybills, and data-driven logistics, and those expectations are shaping how hubs operate across Europe. Michael Zach, Senior Vice President, Ground Handling and Cargo Operations at Vienna Airport, put it plainly: “We see digitalisation accelerating across the industry — real-time visibility, e-AWB, and data-driven decision-making are now expected by our customers and are no longer optional.
**For more on this:**https://aircargoweek.com/european-airfreight-finds-its-footing/
**For more general reading:**https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Air_freight_transport_statistics
**John Stewart May 2026**

**Belgium ranked as the EU's third-largest country for air freight in 2025, overtaking several larger member states as cargo volumes rose sharply, according to figures published by Statbel on Thursday.**
More than two million tonnes of freight and mail passed through Belgian airports last year, an increase of almost 13% compared with 2024.
Only Germany, with 4.8 million tonnes, and France, with 2.2 million tonnes, handled more air cargo. Belgium, driven primarily by Liège Airport and Brucargo at Brussels Airport, ranked ahead of the Netherlands (1.4 million tonnes), Spain (1.3 million tonnes) and Italy (1.2 million tonnes).
Passenger traffic also reached a record high, with just over 36 million travellers using Belgian airports in 2025, up 3.6% from the previous year. The figure surpassed the pre-pandemic record of 35.5 million passengers set in 2019 and placed Belgium 12th among EU member states for passenger traffic.
Across the European Union, more than one billion passengers travelled through airports last year, with Spain, Germany, Italy and France recording the highest passenger volumes.

## Highlights
Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
In 2024, 14.3 million tonnes of freight and mail were transported by air in the EU.
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport for freight and mail, with 2.0 million tonnes.
Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
This article analyses recent freight and mail data on air transport in the European Union (EU), EFTA countries and 4 of the candidate countries, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Türkiye. The role of air transport in freight transport is less significant than in passenger transport, as aircraft are an expensive transport mode in terms of tonne-kilometres and only competitive for longer distances and relatively light high-value or perishable goods.
The article distinguishes between national (domestic), intra- and extra-EU transport, then examines the significance and ranking of airports.

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Total freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% in 2024 compared with 2023 (Table 1), reaching 14.3 million tonnes. This increase was mainly due to intra -EU transport which grew by 9.1%, while extra-EU was relatively stable (+0.1%). In contrast, national transport decreased by 4.3%.
Between 2023 and 2024, freight and mail transport by air increased in all EU countries, except Poland (-3.6%) and Latvia (-2.7%). Among the EFTA and candidate countries, only Iceland recorded a decrease (-2.3%). The highest increase was registered by Hungary (+65.9%), followed by Czechia (+43.7%), Greece (+36.7%) and Cyprus (+20.1%). Among the remaining EU countries, 11 recorded a growth between 10% an 15%. Noticeable increases were also recorded in the EFTA countries Norway (+27.5%) and Switzerland (+14.6%) as well as in all candidate countries, North Macedonia showing the highest, with +92.3%.
In 2024, the highest volume of freight and mail was loaded and unloaded at German airports, with 4.7 million tonnes. Belgium, Spain, France, Italy, the Netherlands and the candidate country Türkiye were the other countries with more than 1 million tonnes of freight and mail loaded and unloaded in 2024.
Table 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Figure 1 indicates that the extra-EU transport represented 83.3% of the total air freight and mail transport. It was the main origin/destination far ahead of intra-EU transport (13.9%) and national transport (2.9%). Compared with 2023, intra-EU and national transport lost 1.2 percentage points (pp) and 0.4 pp in 2024, respectively, to the benefit of extra-EU.
Figure 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Map 1 gives a picture of the extra-EU market. Eastern Asia was the main origin/destination of freight and mail transported by air in 2024, with 25.4% of the total extra-EU transport, followed by North America (21.5%). The lowest share was observed for Australasia, S. Sea Is. & Antarctica (0.03%). Decreases were observed in transport with Central America and Caribbean (-6.4%), rest of Africa (Africa without Eastern Africa) (-0.9%) and Northern America (-0.4%). By contrast, transport with the other world regions increased between 2023 and 2024. In relative terms, the highest growths were recorded for transport with Central Asia (+47.5%), Western Asia (+24.4%), Oceania and southern polar regions (+18.5%), South eastern Asia (+13.4%) and Eastern Asia (+12.8%).
Map 1: Extra-EU air freight and mail transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ (avia_goexcc)
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport in terms of tonnes of freight and mail loaded/unloaded, with 2.0 million tonnes, closely followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle, with 1.9 million tonnes (Table 2). Amsterdam Schiphol, Leipzig Halle and Liege were the other EU airports with more than 1 million tonnes in 2024. When looking at the number of flights, the ranking was slightly different. Leipzig Halle was first with 49 948 flights, followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle (38 071 flights), Köln Bonn (34 706 flights), Liege (24 334 flights), Frankfurt Main (23 743 flights) and Milano Malpensa (22 975 flights). These were the only airports with more than 20 000 flights.

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Among the top 20 airports, 18 registered a growth between 2023 and 2024 in terms of total freight and mail loaded/unloaded. Budapest Liszt Ferenc International recorded the highest increase (+65.7%), followed by Roma Fiumicino (+44.4%), Zaragoza (+39.6%) and Liege (+20.4%). In addition, 6 airports recorded a growth between 10% and 20%. By contrast, Köln Bonn (-3.5%) and Leipzig Halle (-0.6%) recorded a decrease between 2023 and 2024.
Table 2: Top EU airports for freight and mail transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooa)
Figure 2 presents freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class. For long distances over 2 000 km, 99% of the total transport was extra-EU in 2024, 2023 and 2022. For distances between 1 500 and 1 999 km, extra-EU transport represented 58% of the total in 2024 and 2022. In 2023, this share was 55%. Intra-EU transport of freight and mail was predominant in distances inferior to 1 500 km. In 2024, it represented 73% of total transport in the 1 000–1 499 km distance class, 69% in 500–999 km class and 51% in 300–499 km class. When looking at distances lower than 300 km, intra-EU transport represented 53%, while national claimed 39% of the total freight and mail on board.
Figure 2: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class, EU, 2022, 2023 and 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_goodis)

**European Air Freight**
**83% of the freight using European airports is from outside Europe.** Intra-EU freight made up only 13.9% and national freight just 2.9%.
The role of air transport in freight transport is less significant than in passenger transport as air is expensive and only competitive with road and rail for longer distances and relatively light high-value or perishable goods.
Nevertheless, total freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% in 2024 compared with 2023, reaching 14.3 million tonnes. This increase was mainly due to intra-EU transport which grew by 9.1%, while extra-EU was relatively stable (+0.1%). In contrast, national transport decreased by 4.3%.
**The American market dominates but the fastest-growing was the Asian market.**
**The highest volume of freight and mail was loaded and unloaded at German airports, with 4.7 million tonnes**. Belgium, Spain, France, Italy, the Netherlands and Turkey were the other countries with more than 1 million tonnes of freight and mail. UK airports, not included in the table below, handled approximately 2.8 million tonnes of air freight in 2024.
**Frankfurt was the main EU airport for freight and mail, with 2.0 million tonnes.**It was closely followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle, with 1.9 million tonnes. Amsterdam Schiphol, Leipzig Halle and Liege were the other EU airports with more than 1 million tonnes in 2024. Heathrow, if it had been included in the table would have been in 3rd place with 1.59 million tonnes of cargo,
**When looking at the number of flights, the ranking was slightly different**. Leipzig Halle was first with 49 948 flights, followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle (38 071 flights), Köln Bonn (34 706 flights), Liege (24 334 flights), Frankfurt Main (23 743 flights) and Milano Malpensa (22 975 flights). These were the only airports with more than 20 000 flights.

A main reason for this is, while major hubs like London Heathrow, Frankfurt, and Paris-CDG are highly reliant on belly-hold, specialist airports like Liège are driven by dedicated freighters. Overall belly-hold cargo capacity has continued to grow, accounting for roughly 55.5% of total international freight as of September 2025, with dedicated freighters taking the remainder.
**At the specialist freight airports more than 40% of all-cargo flights in Europe operate between 11 p.m. and 7 a.m.** While freighter aircraft represent only around 3% of total European traffic, they are heavily concentrated at night, particularly between midnight and 5 a.m. at around 25 key cargo-focused airports. (Eurocontrol, https://www.eurocontrol.int/archive_download/all/node/10576 )
**Future trends**
European air freight is entering a more complex phase, with modest demand growth offset by rising expectations around digitalisation, real-time visibility, and regulatory compliance. Competitive dynamics are shifting as airlines increasingly favour secondary hubs over congested mega-hubs, prioritising efficiency, resilience, and seamless data integration in response to geopolitical and supply chain risks. Vienna Airport exemplifies this trend, leveraging speed, strong Central and Eastern Europe connectivity, and continuous investment in digital and operational efficiency to position itself as a high-performance alternative, reflected in record cargo volumes and broad-based growth. Efficiency, compliance, and digital tools are no longer just nice-to-haves—they are now central to staying competitive. Customers expect real-time updates, electronic air waybills, and data-driven logistics, and those expectations are shaping how hubs operate across Europe. Title: Air freight transport statistics
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5
Data extracted in December 2025
Planned article update: 7 December 2026

## Highlights
Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
In 2024, 14.3 million tonnes of freight and mail were transported by air in the EU.
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport for freight and mail, with 2.0 million tonnes.
Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
This article analyses recent freight and mail data on air transport in the European Union (EU), EFTA countries and 4 of the candidate countries, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Türkiye. The role of air transport in freight transport is less significant than in passenger transport, as aircraft are an expensive transport mode in terms of tonne-kilometres and only competitive for longer distances and relatively light high-value or perishable goods.
The article distinguishes between national (domestic), intra- and extra-EU transport, then examines the significance and ranking of airports.

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Total freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% in 2024 compared with 2023 (Table 1), reaching 14.3 million tonnes. This increase was mainly due to intra -EU transport which grew by 9.1%, while extra-EU was relatively stable (+0.1%). In contrast, national transport decreased by 4.3%.
Between 2023 and 2024, freight and mail transport by air increased in all EU countries, except Poland (-3.6%) and Latvia (-2.7%). Among the EFTA and candidate countries, only Iceland recorded a decrease (-2.3%). The highest increase was registered by Hungary (+65.9%), followed by Czechia (+43.7%), Greece (+36.7%) and Cyprus (+20.1%). Among the remaining EU countries, 11 recorded a growth between 10% an 15%. Noticeable increases were also recorded in the EFTA countries Norway (+27.5%) and Switzerland (+14.6%) as well as in all candidate countries, North Macedonia showing the highest, with +92.3%.
In 2024, the highest volume of freight and mail was loaded and unloaded at German airports, with 4.7 million tonnes. Belgium, Spain, France, Italy, the Netherlands and the candidate country Türkiye were the other countries with more than 1 million tonnes of freight and mail loaded and unloaded in 2024.
Table 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Figure 1 indicates that the extra-EU transport represented 83.3% of the total air freight and mail transport. It was the main origin/destination far ahead of intra-EU transport (13.9%) and national transport (2.9%). Compared with 2023, intra-EU and national transport lost 1.2 percentage points (pp) and 0.4 pp in 2024, respectively, to the benefit of extra-EU.
Figure 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Map 1 gives a picture of the extra-EU market. Eastern Asia was the main origin/destination of freight and mail transported by air in 2024, with 25.4% of the total extra-EU transport, followed by North America (21.5%). The lowest share was observed for Australasia, S. Sea Is. & Antarctica (0.03%). Decreases were observed in transport with Central America and Caribbean (-6.4%), rest of Africa (Africa without Eastern Africa) (-0.9%) and Northern America (-0.4%). By contrast, transport with the other world regions increased between 2023 and 2024. In relative terms, the highest growths were recorded for transport with Central Asia (+47.5%), Western Asia (+24.4%), Oceania and southern polar regions (+18.5%), South eastern Asia (+13.4%) and Eastern Asia (+12.8%).
Map 1: Extra-EU air freight and mail transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ (avia_goexcc)
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport in terms of tonnes of freight and mail loaded/unloaded, with 2.0 million tonnes, closely followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle, with 1.9 million tonnes (Table 2). Amsterdam Schiphol, Leipzig Halle and Liege were the other EU airports with more than 1 million tonnes in 2024. When looking at the number of flights, the ranking was slightly different. Leipzig Halle was first with 49 948 flights, followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle (38 071 flights), Köln Bonn (34 706 flights), Liege (24 334 flights), Frankfurt Main (23 743 flights) and Milano Malpensa (22 975 flights). These were the only airports with more than 20 000 flights.

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Among the top 20 airports, 18 registered a growth between 2023 and 2024 in terms of total freight and mail loaded/unloaded. Budapest Liszt Ferenc International recorded the highest increase (+65.7%), followed by Roma Fiumicino (+44.4%), Zaragoza (+39.6%) and Liege (+20.4%). In addition, 6 airports recorded a growth between 10% and 20%. By contrast, Köln Bonn (-3.5%) and Leipzig Halle (-0.6%) recorded a decrease between 2023 and 2024.
Table 2: Top EU airports for freight and mail transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooa)
Figure 2 presents freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class. For long distances over 2 000 km, 99% of the total transport was extra-EU in 2024, 2023 and 2022. For distances between 1 500 and 1 999 km, extra-EU transport represented 58% of the total in 2024 and 2022. In 2023, this share was 55%. Intra-EU transport of freight and mail was predominant in distances inferior to 1 500 km. In 2024, it represented 73% of total transport in the 1 000–1 499 km distance class, 69% in 500–999 km class and 51% in 300–499 km class. When looking at distances lower than 300 km, intra-EU transport represented 53%, while national claimed 39% of the total freight and mail on board.
Figure 2: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class, EU, 2022, 2023 and 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_goodis)

Map 1: Extra-EU air freight and mail transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ (avia_goexcc)
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport in terms of tonnes of freight and mail loaded/unloaded, with 2.0 million tonnes, closely followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle, with 1.9 million tonnes (Table 2). Amsterdam Schiphol, Leipzig Halle and Liege were the other EU airports with more than 1 million tonnes in 2024. When looking at the number of flights, the ranking was slightly different. Leipzig Halle was first with 49 948 flights, followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle (38 071 flights), Köln Bonn (34 706 flights), Liege (24 334 flights), Frankfurt Main (23 743 flights) and Milano Malpensa (22 975 flights). These were the only airports with more than 20 000 flights.
texts.4:
## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Among the top 20 airports, 18 registered a growth between 2023 and 2024 in terms of total freight and mail loaded/unloaded. Budapest Liszt Ferenc International recorded the highest increase (+65.7%), followed by Roma Fiumicino (+44.4%), Zaragoza (+39.6%) and Liege (+20.4%). In addition, 6 airports recorded a growth between 10% and 20%. By contrast, Köln Bonn (-3.5%) and Leipzig Halle (-0.6%) recorded a decrease between 2023 and 2024.
Table 2: Top EU airports for freight and mail transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooa)
Figure 2 presents freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class. For long distances over 2 000 km, 99% of the total transport was extra-EU in 2024, 2023 and 2022. For distances between 1 500 and 1 999 km, extra-EU transport represented 58% of the total in 2024 and 2022. In 2023, this share was 55%. Intra-EU transport of freight and mail was predominant in distances inferior to 1 500 km. In 2024, it represented 73% of total transport in the 1 000–1 499 km distance class, 69% in 500–999 km class and 51% in 300–499 km class. When looking at distances lower than 300 km, intra-EU transport represented 53%, while national claimed 39% of the total freight and mail on board.
Figure 2: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class, EU, 2022, 2023 and 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_goodis)

## Highlights
Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
In 2024, 14.3 million tonnes of freight and mail were transported by air in the EU.
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport for freight and mail, with 2.0 million tonnes.
Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
This article analyses recent freight and mail data on air transport in the European Union (EU), EFTA countries and 4 of the candidate countries, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Türkiye. The role of air transport in freight transport is less significant than in passenger transport, as aircraft are an expensive transport mode in terms of tonne-kilometres and only competitive for longer distances and relatively light high-value or perishable goods.
The article distinguishes between national (domestic), intra- and extra-EU transport, then examines the significance and ranking of airports.

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Total freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% in 2024 compared with 2023 (Table 1), reaching 14.3 million tonnes. This increase was mainly due to intra -EU transport which grew by 9.1%, while extra-EU was relatively stable (+0.1%). In contrast, national transport decreased by 4.3%.
Between 2023 and 2024, freight and mail transport by air increased in all EU countries, except Poland (-3.6%) and Latvia (-2.7%). Among the EFTA and candidate countries, only Iceland recorded a decrease (-2.3%). The highest increase was registered by Hungary (+65.9%), followed by Czechia (+43.7%), Greece (+36.7%) and Cyprus (+20.1%). Among the remaining EU countries, 11 recorded a growth between 10% an 15%. Noticeable increases were also recorded in the EFTA countries Norway (+27.5%) and Switzerland (+14.6%) as well as in all candidate countries, North Macedonia showing the highest, with +92.3%.
In 2024, the highest volume of freight and mail was loaded and unloaded at German airports, with 4.7 million tonnes. Belgium, Spain, France, Italy, the Netherlands and the candidate country Türkiye were the other countries with more than 1 million tonnes of freight and mail loaded and unloaded in 2024.
Table 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Figure 1 indicates that the extra-EU transport represented 83.3% of the total air freight and mail transport. It was the main origin/destination far ahead of intra-EU transport (13.9%) and national transport (2.9%). Compared with 2023, intra-EU and national transport lost 1.2 percentage points (pp) and 0.4 pp in 2024, respectively, to the benefit of extra-EU.
Figure 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Map 1 gives a picture of the extra-EU market. Eastern Asia was the main origin/destination of freight and mail transported by air in 2024, with 25.4% of the total extra-EU transport, followed by North America (21.5%). The lowest share was observed for Australasia, S. Sea Is. & Antarctica (0.03%). Decreases were observed in transport with Central America and Caribbean (-6.4%), rest of Africa (Africa without Eastern Africa) (-0.9%) and Northern America (-0.4%). By contrast, transport with the other world regions increased between 2023 and 2024. In relative terms, the highest growths were recorded for transport with Central Asia (+47.5%), Western Asia (+24.4%), Oceania and southern polar regions (+18.5%), South eastern Asia (+13.4%) and Eastern Asia (+12.8%).
Map 1: Extra-EU air freight and mail transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ (avia_goexcc)
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport in terms of tonnes of freight and mail loaded/unloaded, with 2.0 million tonnes, closely followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle, with 1.9 million tonnes (Table 2). Amsterdam Schiphol, Leipzig Halle and Liege were the other EU airports with more than 1 million tonnes in 2024. When looking at the number of flights, the ranking was slightly different. Leipzig Halle was first with 49 948 flights, followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle (38 071 flights), Köln Bonn (34 706 flights), Liege (24 334 flights), Frankfurt Main (23 743 flights) and Milano Malpensa (22 975 flights). These were the only airports with more than 20 000 flights.

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Among the top 20 airports, 18 registered a growth between 2023 and 2024 in terms of total freight and mail loaded/unloaded. Budapest Liszt Ferenc International recorded the highest increase (+65.7%), followed by Roma Fiumicino (+44.4%), Zaragoza (+39.6%) and Liege (+20.4%). In addition, 6 airports recorded a growth between 10% and 20%. By contrast, Köln Bonn (-3.5%) and Leipzig Halle (-0.6%) recorded a decrease between 2023 and 2024.

_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooa)

Intra-EU transport of freight and mail was predominant in distances inferior to 1 500 km. In 2024, it represented 73% of total transport in the 1 000–1 499 km distance class, 69% in 500–999 km class and 51% in 300–499 km class. When looking at distances lower than 300 km, intra-EU transport represented 53%, while national claimed 39% of the total freight and mail on board.

## Highlights
Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
In 2024, 14.3 million tonnes of freight and mail were transported by air in the EU.
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport for freight and mail, with 2.0 million tonnes.
Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
This article analyses recent freight and mail data on air transport in the European Union (EU), EFTA countries and 4 of the candidate countries, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Türkiye. The role of air transport in freight transport is less significant than in passenger transport, as aircraft are an expensive transport mode in terms of tonne-kilometres and only competitive for longer distances and relatively light high-value or perishable goods.
The article distinguishes between national (domestic), intra- and extra-EU transport, then examines the significance and ranking of airports.

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Total freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% in 2024 compared with 2023 (Table 1), reaching 14.3 million tonnes. This increase was mainly due to intra -EU transport which grew by 9.1%, while extra-EU was relatively stable (+0.1%). In contrast, national transport decreased by 4.3%.
Between 2023 and 2024, freight and mail transport by air increased in all EU countries, except Poland (-3.6%) and Latvia (-2.7%). Among the EFTA and candidate countries, only Iceland recorded a decrease (-2.3%). The highest increase was registered by Hungary (+65.9%), followed by Czechia (+43.7%), Greece (+36.7%) and Cyprus (+20.1%). Among the remaining EU countries, 11 recorded a growth between 10% an 15%. Noticeable increases were also recorded in the EFTA countries Norway (+27.5%) and Switzerland (+14.6%) as well as in all candidate countries, North Macedonia showing the highest, with +92.3%.
In 2024, the highest volume of freight and mail was loaded and unloaded at German airports, with 4.7 million tonnes. Belgium, Spain, France, Italy, the Netherlands and the candidate country Türkiye were the other countries with more than 1 million tonnes of freight and mail loaded and unloaded in 2024.
Table 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Figure 1 indicates that the extra-EU transport represented 83.3% of the total air freight and mail transport. It was the main origin/destination far ahead of intra-EU transport (13.9%) and national transport (2.9%). Compared with 2023, intra-EU and national transport lost 1.2 percentage points (pp) and 0.4 pp in 2024, respectively, to the benefit of extra-EU.
Figure 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Map 1 gives a picture of the extra-EU market. Eastern Asia was the main origin/destination of freight and mail transported by air in 2024, with 25.4% of the total extra-EU transport, followed by North America (21.5%). The lowest share was observed for Australasia, S. Sea Is. & Antarctica (0.03%). Decreases were observed in transport with Central America and Caribbean (-6.4%), rest of Africa (Africa without Eastern Africa) (-0.9%) and Northern America (-0.4%). By contrast, transport with the other world regions increased between 2023 and 2024. In relative terms, the highest growths were recorded for transport with Central Asia (+47.5%), Western Asia (+24.4%), Oceania and southern polar regions (+18.5%), South eastern Asia (+13.4%) and Eastern Asia (+12.8%).
Map 1: Extra-EU air freight and mail transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ (avia_goexcc)
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport in terms of tonnes of freight and mail loaded/unloaded, with 2.0 million tonnes, closely followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle, with 1.9 million tonnes (Table 2). Amsterdam Schiphol, Leipzig Halle and Liege were the other EU airports with more than 1 million tonnes in 2024. When looking at the number of flights, the ranking was slightly different. Leipzig Halle was first with 49 948 flights, followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle (38 071 flights), Köln Bonn (34 706 flights), Liege (24 334 flights), Frankfurt Main (23 743 flights) and Milano Malpensa (22 975 flights). These were the only airports with more than 20 000 flights.

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Among the top 20 airports, 18 registered a growth between 2023 and 2024 in terms of total freight and mail loaded/unloaded. Budapest Liszt Ferenc International recorded the highest increase (+65.7%), followed by Roma Fiumicino (+44.4%), Zaragoza (+39.6%) and Liege (+20.4%). In addition, 6 airports recorded a growth between 10% and 20%. By contrast, Köln Bonn (-3.5%) and Leipzig Halle (-0.6%) recorded a decrease between 2023 and 2024.
Table 2: Top EU airports for freight and mail transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooa)
Figure 2 presents freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class. For long distances over 2 000 km, 99% of the total transport was extra-EU in 2024, 2023 and 2022. For distances between 1 500 and 1 999 km, extra-EU transport represented 58% of the total in 2024 and 2022. In 2023, this share was 55%. Intra-EU transport of freight and mail was predominant in distances inferior to 1 500 km. In 2024, it represented 73% of total transport in the 1 000–1 499 km distance class, 69% in 500–999 km class and 51% in 300–499 km class. When looking at distances lower than 300 km, intra-EU transport represented 53%, while national claimed 39% of the total freight and mail on board.
Figure 2: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class, EU, 2022, 2023 and 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_goodis)

texts.1:
## Highlights
Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
In 2024, 14.3 million tonnes of freight and mail were transported by air in the EU.
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport for freight and mail, with 2.0 million tonnes.
Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
This article analyses recent freight and mail data on air transport in the European Union (EU), EFTA countries and 4 of the candidate countries, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Türkiye. The role of air transport in freight transport is less significant than in passenger transport, as aircraft are an expensive transport mode in terms of tonne-kilometres and only competitive for longer distances and relatively light high-value or perishable goods.
The article distinguishes between national (domestic), intra- and extra-EU transport, then examines the significance and ranking of airports.
texts.2:
## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Total freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% in 2024 compared with 2023 (Table 1), reaching 14.3 million tonnes. This increase was mainly due to intra -EU transport which grew by 9.1%, while extra-EU was relatively stable (+0.1%). In contrast, national transport decreased by 4.3%.
Between 2023 and 2024, freight and mail transport by air increased in all EU countries, except Poland (-3.6%) and Latvia (-2.7%). Among the EFTA and candidate countries, only Iceland recorded a decrease (-2.3%). The highest increase was registered by Hungary (+65.9%), followed by Czechia (+43.7%), Greece (+36.7%) and Cyprus (+20.1%). Among the remaining EU countries, 11 recorded a growth between 10% an 15%. Noticeable increases were also recorded in the EFTA countries Norway (+27.5%) and Switzerland (+14.6%) as well as in all candidate countries, North Macedonia showing the highest, with +92.3%.
In 2024, the highest volume of freight and mail was loaded and unloaded at German airports, with 4.7 million tonnes. Belgium, Spain, France, Italy, the Netherlands and the candidate country Türkiye were the other countries with more than 1 million tonnes of freight and mail loaded and unloaded in 2024.
Table 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Figure 1 indicates that the extra-EU transport represented 83.3% of the total air freight and mail transport. It was the main origin/destination far ahead of intra-EU transport (13.9%) and national transport (2.9%). Compared with 2023, intra-EU and national transport lost 1.2 percentage points (pp) and 0.4 pp in 2024, respectively, to the benefit of extra-EU.
Figure 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024
texts.3:
## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Map 1 gives a picture of the extra-EU market. Eastern Asia was the main origin/destination of freight and mail transported by air in 2024, with 25.4% of the total extra-EU transport, followed by North America (21.5%). The lowest share was observed for Australasia, S. Sea Is. & Antarctica (0.03%). Decreases were observed in transport with Central America and Caribbean (-6.4%), rest of Africa (Africa without Eastern Africa) (-0.9%) and Northern America (-0.4%). By contrast, transport with the other world regions increased between 2023 and 2024. In relative terms, the highest growths were recorded for transport with Central Asia (+47.5%), Western Asia (+24.4%), Oceania and southern polar regions (+18.5%), South eastern Asia (+13.4%) and Eastern Asia (+12.8%).
Map 1: Extra-EU air freight and mail transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ (avia_goexcc)
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport in terms of tonnes of freight and mail loaded/unloaded, with 2.0 million tonnes, closely followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle, with 1.9 million tonnes (Table 2). Amsterdam Schiphol, Leipzig Halle and Liege were the other EU airports with more than 1 million tonnes in 2024. When looking at the number of flights, the ranking was slightly different. Leipzig Halle was first with 49 948 flights, followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle (38 071 flights), Köln Bonn (34 706 flights), Liege (24 334 flights), Frankfurt Main (23 743 flights) and Milano Malpensa (22 975 flights). These were the only airports with more than 20 000 flights.
texts.4:
## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Among the top 20 airports, 18 registered a growth between 2023 and 2024 in terms of total freight and mail loaded/unloaded. Budapest Liszt Ferenc International recorded the highest increase (+65.7%), followed by Roma Fiumicino (+44.4%), Zaragoza (+39.6%) and Liege (+20.4%). In addition, 6 airports recorded a growth between 10% and 20%. By contrast, Köln Bonn (-3.5%) and Leipzig Halle (-0.6%) recorded a decrease between 2023 and 2024.
Table 2: Top EU airports for freight and mail transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooa)
Figure 2 presents freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class. For long distances over 2 000 km, 99% of the total transport was extra-EU in 2024, 2023 and 2022. For distances between 1 500 and 1 999 km, extra-EU transport represented 58% of the total in 2024 and 2022. In 2023, this share was 55%. Intra-EU transport of freight and mail was predominant in distances inferior to 1 500 km. In 2024, it represented 73% of total transport in the 1 000–1 499 km distance class, 69% in 500–999 km class and 51% in 300–499 km class. When looking at distances lower than 300 km, intra-EU transport represented 53%, while national claimed 39% of the total freight and mail on board.
Figure 2: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class, EU, 2022, 2023 and 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_goodis)

Title: Air freight transport statistics
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5
Data extracted in December 2025
Planned article update: 7 December 2026

## Highlights
Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
In 2024, 14.3 million tonnes of freight and mail were transported by air in the EU.
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport for freight and mail, with 2.0 million tonnes.
Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
This article analyses recent freight and mail data on air transport in the European Union (EU), EFTA countries and 4 of the candidate countries, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Türkiye. The role of air transport in freight transport is less significant than in passenger transport, as aircraft are an expensive transport mode in terms of tonne-kilometres and only competitive for longer distances and relatively light high-value or perishable goods.
The article distinguishes between national (domestic), intra- and extra-EU transport, then examines the significance and ranking of airports.

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Total freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% in 2024 compared with 2023 (Table 1), reaching 14.3 million tonnes. This increase was mainly due to intra -EU transport which grew by 9.1%, while extra-EU was relatively stable (+0.1%). In contrast, national transport decreased by 4.3%.
Between 2023 and 2024, freight and mail transport by air increased in all EU countries, except Poland (-3.6%) and Latvia (-2.7%). Among the EFTA and candidate countries, only Iceland recorded a decrease (-2.3%). The highest increase was registered by Hungary (+65.9%), followed by Czechia (+43.7%), Greece (+36.7%) and Cyprus (+20.1%). Among the remaining EU countries, 11 recorded a growth between 10% an 15%. Noticeable increases were also recorded in the EFTA countries Norway (+27.5%) and Switzerland (+14.6%) as well as in all candidate countries, North Macedonia showing the highest, with +92.3%.
In 2024, the highest volume of freight and mail was loaded and unloaded at German airports, with 4.7 million tonnes. Belgium, Spain, France, Italy, the Netherlands and the candidate country Türkiye were the other countries with more than 1 million tonnes of freight and mail loaded and unloaded in 2024.
Table 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Figure 1 indicates that the extra-EU transport represented 83.3% of the total air freight and mail transport. It was the main origin/destination far ahead of intra-EU transport (13.9%) and national transport (2.9%). Compared with 2023, intra-EU and national transport lost 1.2 percentage points (pp) and 0.4 pp in 2024, respectively, to the benefit of extra-EU.
Figure 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Map 1 gives a picture of the extra-EU market. Eastern Asia was the main origin/destination of freight and mail transported by air in 2024, with 25.4% of the total extra-EU transport, followed by North America (21.5%). The lowest share was observed for Australasia, S. Sea Is. & Antarctica (0.03%). Decreases were observed in transport with Central America and Caribbean (-6.4%), rest of Africa (Africa without Eastern Africa) (-0.9%) and Northern America (-0.4%). By contrast, transport with the other world regions increased between 2023 and 2024. In relative terms, the highest growths were recorded for transport with Central Asia (+47.5%), Western Asia (+24.4%), Oceania and southern polar regions (+18.5%), South eastern Asia (+13.4%) and Eastern Asia (+12.8%).
Map 1: Extra-EU air freight and mail transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ (avia_goexcc)
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport in terms of tonnes of freight and mail loaded/unloaded, with 2.0 million tonnes, closely followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle, with 1.9 million tonnes (Table 2). Amsterdam Schiphol, Leipzig Halle and Liege were the other EU airports with more than 1 million tonnes in 2024. When looking at the number of flights, the ranking was slightly different. Leipzig Halle was first with 49 948 flights, followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle (38 071 flights), Köln Bonn (34 706 flights), Liege (24 334 flights), Frankfurt Main (23 743 flights) and Milano Malpensa (22 975 flights). These were the only airports with more than 20 000 flights.

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Among the top 20 airports, 18 registered a growth between 2023 and 2024 in terms of total freight and mail loaded/unloaded. Budapest Liszt Ferenc International recorded the highest increase (+65.7%), followed by Roma Fiumicino (+44.4%), Zaragoza (+39.6%) and Liege (+20.4%). In addition, 6 airports recorded a growth between 10% and 20%. By contrast, Köln Bonn (-3.5%) and Leipzig Halle (-0.6%) recorded a decrease between 2023 and 2024.
Table 2: Top EU airports for freight and mail transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooa)
Figure 2 presents freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class. For long distances over 2 000 km, 99% of the total transport was extra-EU in 2024, 2023 and 2022. For distances between 1 500 and 1 999 km, extra-EU transport represented 58% of the total in 2024 and 2022. In 2023, this share was 55%. Intra-EU transport of freight and mail was predominant in distances inferior to 1 500 km. In 2024, it represented 73% of total transport in the 1 000–1 499 km distance class, 69% in 500–999 km class and 51% in 300–499 km class. When looking at distances lower than 300 km, intra-EU transport represented 53%, while national claimed 39% of the total freight and mail on board.
Figure 2: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class, EU, 2022, 2023 and 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_goodis)

## Highlights
Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
In 2024, 14.3 million tonnes of freight and mail were transported by air in the EU.
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport for freight and mail, with 2.0 million tonnes.
Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
This article analyses recent freight and mail data on air transport in the European Union (EU), EFTA countries and 4 of the candidate countries, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Türkiye. The role of air transport in freight transport is less significant than in passenger transport, as aircraft are an expensive transport mode in terms of tonne-kilometres and only competitive for longer distances and relatively light high-value or perishable goods.
The article distinguishes between national (domestic), intra- and extra-EU transport, then examines the significance and ranking of airports.
texts.2:
## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Total freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% in 2024 compared with 2023 (Table 1), reaching 14.3 million tonnes. This increase was mainly due to intra -EU transport which grew by 9.1%, while extra-EU was relatively stable (+0.1%). In contrast, national transport decreased by 4.3%.
Between 2023 and 2024, freight and mail transport by air increased in all EU countries, except Poland (-3.6%) and Latvia (-2.7%). Among the EFTA and candidate countries, only Iceland recorded a decrease (-2.3%). The highest increase was registered by Hungary (+65.9%), followed by Czechia (+43.7%), Greece (+36.7%) and Cyprus (+20.1%). Among the remaining EU countries, 11 recorded a growth between 10% an 15%. Noticeable increases were also recorded in the EFTA countries Norway (+27.5%) and Switzerland (+14.6%) as well as in all candidate countries, North Macedonia showing the highest, with +92.3%.
In 2024, the highest volume of freight and mail was loaded and unloaded at German airports, with 4.7 million tonnes. Belgium, Spain, France, Italy, the Netherlands and the candidate country Türkiye were the other countries with more than 1 million tonnes of freight and mail loaded and unloaded in 2024.
Table 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Figure 1 indicates that the extra-EU transport represented 83.3% of the total air freight and mail transport. It was the main origin/destination far ahead of intra-EU transport (13.9%) and national transport (2.9%). Compared with 2023, intra-EU and national transport lost 1.2 percentage points (pp) and 0.4 pp in 2024, respectively, to the benefit of extra-EU.
Figure 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024
texts.3:
## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Map 1 gives a picture of the extra-EU market. Eastern Asia was the main origin/destination of freight and mail transported by air in 2024, with 25.4% of the total extra-EU transport, followed by North America (21.5%). The lowest share was observed for Australasia, S. Sea Is. & Antarctica (0.03%). Decreases were observed in transport with Central America and Caribbean (-6.4%), rest of Africa (Africa without Eastern Africa) (-0.9%) and Northern America (-0.4%). By contrast, transport with the other world regions increased between 2023 and 2024. In relative terms, the highest growths were recorded for transport with Central Asia (+47.5%), Western Asia (+24.4%), Oceania and southern polar regions (+18.5%), South eastern Asia (+13.4%) and Eastern Asia (+12.8%).
Map 1: Extra-EU air freight and mail transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ (avia_goexcc)
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport in terms of tonnes of freight and mail loaded/unloaded, with 2.0 million tonnes, closely followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle, with 1.9 million tonnes (Table 2). Amsterdam Schiphol, Leipzig Halle and Liege were the other EU airports with more than 1 million tonnes in 2024. When looking at the number of flights, the ranking was slightly different. Leipzig Halle was first with 49 948 flights, followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle (38 071 flights), Köln Bonn (34 706 flights), Liege (24 334 flights), Frankfurt Main (23 743 flights) and Milano Malpensa (22 975 flights). These were the only airports with more than 20 000 flights.
texts.4:
## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Among the top 20 airports, 18 registered a growth between 2023 and 2024 in terms of total freight and mail loaded/unloaded. Budapest Liszt Ferenc International recorded the highest increase (+65.7%), followed by Roma Fiumicino (+44.4%), Zaragoza (+39.6%) and Liege (+20.4%). In addition, 6 airports recorded a growth between 10% and 20%. By contrast, Köln Bonn (-3.5%) and Leipzig Halle (-0.6%) recorded a decrease between 2023 and 2024.
Table 2: Top EU airports for freight and mail transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooa)
Figure 2 presents freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class. For long distances over 2 000 km, 99% of the total transport was extra-EU in 2024, 2023 and 2022. For distances between 1 500 and 1 999 km, extra-EU transport represented 58% of the total in 2024 and 2022. In 2023, this share was 55%. Intra-EU transport of freight and mail was predominant in distances inferior to 1 500 km. In 2024, it represented 73% of total transport in the 1 000–1 499 km distance class, 69% in 500–999 km class and 51% in 300–499 km class. When looking at distances lower than 300 km, intra-EU transport represented 53%, while national claimed 39% of the total freight and mail on board.
Figure 2: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class, EU, 2022, 2023 and 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_goodis)

## Highlights
Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
In 2024, 14.3 million tonnes of freight and mail were transported by air in the EU.
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport for freight and mail, with 2.0 million tonnes.
Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
This article analyses recent freight and mail data on air transport in the European Union (EU), EFTA countries and 4 of the candidate countries, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Türkiye. The role of air transport in freight transport is less significant than in passenger transport, as aircraft are an expensive transport mode in terms of tonne-kilometres and only competitive for longer distances and relatively light high-value or perishable goods.
The article distinguishes between national (domestic), intra- and extra-EU transport, then examines the significance and ranking of airports.

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Total freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% in 2024 compared with 2023 (Table 1), reaching 14.3 million tonnes. This increase was mainly due to intra -EU transport which grew by 9.1%, while extra-EU was relatively stable (+0.1%). In contrast, national transport decreased by 4.3%.
Between 2023 and 2024, freight and mail transport by air increased in all EU countries, except Poland (-3.6%) and Latvia (-2.7%). Among the EFTA and candidate countries, only Iceland recorded a decrease (-2.3%). The highest increase was registered by Hungary (+65.9%), followed by Czechia (+43.7%), Greece (+36.7%) and Cyprus (+20.1%). Among the remaining EU countries, 11 recorded a growth between 10% an 15%. Noticeable increases were also recorded in the EFTA countries Norway (+27.5%) and Switzerland (+14.6%) as well as in all candidate countries, North Macedonia showing the highest, with +92.3%.
In 2024, the highest volume of freight and mail was loaded and unloaded at German airports, with 4.7 million tonnes. Belgium, Spain, France, Italy, the Netherlands and the candidate country Türkiye were the other countries with more than 1 million tonnes of freight and mail loaded and unloaded in 2024.
Table 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Figure 1 indicates that the extra-EU transport represented 83.3% of the total air freight and mail transport. It was the main origin/destination far ahead of intra-EU transport (13.9%) and national transport (2.9%). Compared with 2023, intra-EU and national transport lost 1.2 percentage points (pp) and 0.4 pp in 2024, respectively, to the benefit of extra-EU.
Figure 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Map 1 gives a picture of the extra-EU market. Eastern Asia was the main origin/destination of freight and mail transported by air in 2024, with 25.4% of the total extra-EU transport, followed by North America (21.5%). The lowest share was observed for Australasia, S. Sea Is. & Antarctica (0.03%). Decreases were observed in transport with Central America and Caribbean (-6.4%), rest of Africa (Africa without Eastern Africa) (-0.9%) and Northern America (-0.4%). By contrast, transport with the other world regions increased between 2023 and 2024. In relative terms, the highest growths were recorded for transport with Central Asia (+47.5%), Western Asia (+24.4%), Oceania and southern polar regions (+18.5%), South eastern Asia (+13.4%) and Eastern Asia (+12.8%).
Map 1: Extra-EU air freight and mail transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ (avia_goexcc)
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport in terms of tonnes of freight and mail loaded/unloaded, with 2.0 million tonnes, closely followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle, with 1.9 million tonnes (Table 2). Amsterdam Schiphol, Leipzig Halle and Liege were the other EU airports with more than 1 million tonnes in 2024. When looking at the number of flights, the ranking was slightly different. Leipzig Halle was first with 49 948 flights, followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle (38 071 flights), Köln Bonn (34 706 flights), Liege (24 334 flights), Frankfurt Main (23 743 flights) and Milano Malpensa (22 975 flights). These were the only airports with more than 20 000 flights.

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Among the top 20 airports, 18 registered a growth between 2023 and 2024 in terms of total freight and mail loaded/unloaded. Budapest Liszt Ferenc International recorded the highest increase (+65.7%), followed by Roma Fiumicino (+44.4%), Zaragoza (+39.6%) and Liege (+20.4%). In addition, 6 airports recorded a growth between 10% and 20%. By contrast, Köln Bonn (-3.5%) and Leipzig Halle (-0.6%) recorded a decrease between 2023 and 2024.
Table 2: Top EU airports for freight and mail transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooa)
Figure 2 presents freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class. For long distances over 2 000 km, 99% of the total transport was extra-EU in 2024, 2023 and 2022. For distances between 1 500 and 1 999 km, extra-EU transport represented 58% of the total in 2024 and 2022. In 2023, this share was 55%. Intra-EU transport of freight and mail was predominant in distances inferior to 1 500 km. In 2024, it represented 73% of total transport in the 1 000–1 499 km distance class, 69% in 500–999 km class and 51% in 300–499 km class. When looking at distances lower than 300 km, intra-EU transport represented 53%, while national claimed 39% of the total freight and mail on board.
Figure 2: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class, EU, 2022, 2023 and 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_goodis)

More than two million tonnes of freight and mail passed through Belgian airports last year, an increase of almost 13% compared with 2024.
Only Germany, with 4.8 million tonnes, and France, with 2.2 million tonnes, handled more air cargo. Belgium, driven primarily by Liège Airport and Brucargo at Brussels Airport, ranked ahead of the Netherlands (1.4 million tonnes), Spain (1.3 million tonnes) and Italy (1.2 million tonnes).
Passenger traffic also reached a record high, with just over 36 million travellers using Belgian airports in 2025, up 3.6% from the previous year. The figure surpassed the pre-pandemic record of 35.5 million passengers set in 2019 and placed Belgium 12th among EU member states for passenger traffic.
Across the European Union, more than one billion passengers travelled through airports last year, with Spain, Germany, Italy and France recording the highest passenger volumes.

**Belgium ranked as the EU's third-largest country for air freight in 2025, overtaking several larger member states as cargo volumes rose sharply, according to figures published by Statbel on Thursday.**

Source: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Air_freight_transport_statistics
Title: Air freight transport statistics
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5
Data extracted in December 2025
Planned article update: 7 December 2026

## Highlights
Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
In 2024, 14.3 million tonnes of freight and mail were transported by air in the EU.
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport for freight and mail, with 2.0 million tonnes.
Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
This article analyses recent freight and mail data on air transport in the European Union (EU), EFTA countries and 4 of the candidate countries, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Türkiye. The role of air transport in freight transport is less significant than in passenger transport, as aircraft are an expensive transport mode in terms of tonne-kilometres and only competitive for longer distances and relatively light high-value or perishable goods.
The article distinguishes between national (domestic), intra- and extra-EU transport, then examines the significance and ranking of airports.

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Total freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% in 2024 compared with 2023 (Table 1), reaching 14.3 million tonnes. This increase was mainly due to intra -EU transport which grew by 9.1%, while extra-EU was relatively stable (+0.1%). In contrast, national transport decreased by 4.3%.
Between 2023 and 2024, freight and mail transport by air increased in all EU countries, except Poland (-3.6%) and Latvia (-2.7%). Among the EFTA and candidate countries, only Iceland recorded a decrease (-2.3%). The highest increase was registered by Hungary (+65.9%), followed by Czechia (+43.7%), Greece (+36.7%) and Cyprus (+20.1%). Among the remaining EU countries, 11 recorded a growth between 10% an 15%. Noticeable increases were also recorded in the EFTA countries Norway (+27.5%) and Switzerland (+14.6%) as well as in all candidate countries, North Macedonia showing the highest, with +92.3%.
In 2024, the highest volume of freight and mail was loaded and unloaded at German airports, with 4.7 million tonnes. Belgium, Spain, France, Italy, the Netherlands and the candidate country Türkiye were the other countries with more than 1 million tonnes of freight and mail loaded and unloaded in 2024.
Table 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Figure 1 indicates that the extra-EU transport represented 83.3% of the total air freight and mail transport. It was the main origin/destination far ahead of intra-EU transport (13.9%) and national transport (2.9%). Compared with 2023, intra-EU and national transport lost 1.2 percentage points (pp) and 0.4 pp in 2024, respectively, to the benefit of extra-EU.
Figure 1: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport, EU, 2024

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooc)
Map 1 gives a picture of the extra-EU market. Eastern Asia was the main origin/destination of freight and mail transported by air in 2024, with 25.4% of the total extra-EU transport, followed by North America (21.5%). The lowest share was observed for Australasia, S. Sea Is. & Antarctica (0.03%). Decreases were observed in transport with Central America and Caribbean (-6.4%), rest of Africa (Africa without Eastern Africa) (-0.9%) and Northern America (-0.4%). By contrast, transport with the other world regions increased between 2023 and 2024. In relative terms, the highest growths were recorded for transport with Central Asia (+47.5%), Western Asia (+24.4%), Oceania and southern polar regions (+18.5%), South eastern Asia (+13.4%) and Eastern Asia (+12.8%).
Map 1: Extra-EU air freight and mail transport, EU, 2024
_Source:_ (avia_goexcc)
In 2024, Frankfurt Main was the main EU airport in terms of tonnes of freight and mail loaded/unloaded, with 2.0 million tonnes, closely followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle, with 1.9 million tonnes (Table 2). Amsterdam Schiphol, Leipzig Halle and Liege were the other EU airports with more than 1 million tonnes in 2024. When looking at the number of flights, the ranking was slightly different. Leipzig Halle was first with 49 948 flights, followed by Paris Charles de Gaulle (38 071 flights), Köln Bonn (34 706 flights), Liege (24 334 flights), Frankfurt Main (23 743 flights) and Milano Malpensa (22 975 flights). These were the only airports with more than 20 000 flights.

## Air freight and mail transport in the EU increased by 8.7% between 2023 and 2024
Among the top 20 airports, 18 registered a growth between 2023 and 2024 in terms of total freight and mail loaded/unloaded. Budapest Liszt Ferenc International recorded the highest increase (+65.7%), followed by Roma Fiumicino (+44.4%), Zaragoza (+39.6%) and Liege (+20.4%). In addition, 6 airports recorded a growth between 10% and 20%. By contrast, Köln Bonn (-3.5%) and Leipzig Halle (-0.6%) recorded a decrease between 2023 and 2024.
Table 2: Top EU airports for freight and mail transport, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (avia_gooa)
Figure 2 presents freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class. For long distances over 2 000 km, 99% of the total transport was extra-EU in 2024, 2023 and 2022. For distances between 1 500 and 1 999 km, extra-EU transport represented 58% of the total in 2024 and 2022. In 2023, this share was 55%. Intra-EU transport of freight and mail was predominant in distances inferior to 1 500 km. In 2024, it represented 73% of total transport in the 1 000–1 499 km distance class, 69% in 500–999 km class and 51% in 300–499 km class. When looking at distances lower than 300 km, intra-EU transport represented 53%, while national claimed 39% of the total freight and mail on board.
Figure 2: Air freight and mail transport by type of transport and distance class, EU, 2022, 2023 and 2024
